parameters.content:
## Error handler
Runs whenever a workflow with `errorWorkflow` set to this one fails, including a trigger or activation error, which carries no `execution` key. Reads config itself (not through a sub-workflow), then emails the operator a plain-text alert in the team's language (`team_locale`) naming the failed node, the error, the execution URL, and the time in Bogota. This workflow carries no `errorWorkflow` of its own, so a failure here does not loop back into itself.

## Compose and send the alert
`Alert input` hands `Compose alert` the config, the Error Trigger's own output (`$('On workflow error').first().json`, since `$json` here is `{ config }`), and the Bogota time, so the Code node stays free of the clock. `Compose alert` writes the alert in `team_locale`, falling back to English with a note when it's invalid, and covers an activation error, which has no `execution` key. `Email operator` sends its `to`, `subject`, and `text` as plain text.

parameters.jsonOutput: ={{ { config: $json.config, failure: $('On workflow error').first().json, time: $now.setZone('America/Bogota').toFormat('yyyy-LL-dd HH:mm') } }}

nodes.name: Compose alert
nodes.notes: Why Code: one tested function picks the team's language and builds the alert from either error payload shape, execution or trigger, instead of an inline expression per field
